record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; source files and other listed documents were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal and capability outcomes for a rank-1 residual-direction weight edit, testing practical refusal removal with a different implementation from activation ablation.
record.gate_note: Rows record only results explicitly reported in the README. The listed scripts and artifacts were not independently inspected or run. Direction-selection settings and reproduction commands are not outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The repo applies a rank-1 residual-direction weight edit to a released 1-bit model (Bonsai-27B, from Qwen3.6-27B). It reports refusal counts before and after, so it bears on V2 in a new setting: extreme quantization. T3 fits better than T2 because the method is essentially abliteration packaged as a LoRA; the new element is the quantized setting.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors present the LoRA adapter as the validated primary release and the mixed Q1_0/Q2_0 merge as a prerelease pending HarmBench. They call their tests useful but limited and not a HarmBench result. They also report that fully Q1_0 requantization erased the effect.
record.recipe_differences: A rank-1 projected residual-direction edit is converted to a LoRA adapter affecting 78 modules, with a separate mixed-quantization standalone merge. The README does not state the original difference-in-means derivation or report activation ablation/addition.
record.method_sensitivity: Quantization affects the reported outcome: the mixed Q1_0/Q2_0 candidate retained the effect, while the fully Q1_0 standalone merge reverted.
record.problems: Evidence is README-reported and was not independently checked. The reported prompt sets are limited marker fixtures, with no uncertainty estimates; the README says results are not a HarmBench evaluation. Capability evidence is limited to benign-prompt manual review and generation speed.

untested.parts: Broad refusal benchmarks (the README says the tests are not HarmBench). Quantitative capability benchmarks. Multiple released models. The full details in RESULTS.md, including 'known regressions', were not read.
Direction derivation (difference-in-means not stated), activation ablation, and direction addition to induce refusal.
Reasoning was turned off at runtime (--reasoning off), so reasoning-mode behavior is untested.

missing.what: Long-context check: the adapter processed an 11,484-token prompt at 16K context and recovered the exact canary.
Full results and 'known regressions' referenced in RESULTS.md, which was not read.

record.verdict_notes: Hobbyist repo, not peer reviewed, README-only evidence. There are no uncertainty estimates and the n is small (12 to 72 prompts). The quantization-sensitivity finding (the edit is lost at 1-bit precision) is the most distinctive result for V2.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not state that the direction was found by harmful-minus-harmless mean activations, nor test activation ablation at every layer and position or direction addition.
Tests target and benign marker refusals on the stated held-out and exact-runtime fixtures, not a broad refusal benchmark; the README says the tests are not a HarmBench result.
No jailbreak attack or training against ablation is reported.
No comparison of a single direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts is reported.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision is tested.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models is tested.
No comparison of refusal training methods or timing is reported.
